nodes.label: Zero jitter under high loss indicates ICMP deprioritization, not real packet loss
nodes.norm_label: zero jitter under high loss indicates icmp deprioritization not real packet loss
nodes.summary: The transcript's central diagnostic finding. The upstream edge router 103.90.249.247 showed 22 percent loss while its RTT stayed locked at 42 ms with roughly 0.5 ms jitter, and the VPS itself measured 16.7 percent. Queue overflow always raises jitter, so a high-loss hop with flat RTT is read as control-plane policing of ICMP rather than packets genuinely going missing. The note is explicit that this is still an inference: separating 'ICMP discarded' from 'data actually lost' requires a TCP-level test such as scp with ss -ti retrans counters, and the agent had locked itself out before it could run one.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - koneksi-vps-banyak-packet-loss [ses_f1c7fa998ffeaX7rILtty0alcT].md:L01212] Pola loss-tinggi-tapi-jitter-nol itu ciri khas router yang **mendeprioritaskan ICMP**, bukan paket yang benar-benar hilang.

nodes.label: Self-inflicted fail2ban lockout from a 25-connection TCP burst
nodes.norm_label: self inflicted fail2ban lockout from a connect burst
nodes.summary: The agent's own diagnostic cost it access. Testing TCP at scale it sent 25 connections to port 22 within seconds; 12 failed and then every TCP port from its IP (22/80/443/3306/5432/8080/8443) returned Connection refused while ICMP still worked, which is a per-IP block inside the VPS, i.e. fail2ban. It then could not SSH in to turn fail2ban off, because the network it had blocked was its own way in. The user asked for a whitelist rather than disabling fail2ban outright. The agent's public IP was 182.10.168.104 on Telkomsel, flagged as possibly dynamic CGNAT, which makes a permanent ignoreip entry a durability question.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - koneksi-vps-banyak-packet-loss [ses_f1c7fa998ffeaX7rILtty0alcT].md:L1221] Gejalanya persis blok per-IP sisi VPS = fail2ban, dan Gw yang bikin access SSH Gw sendiri mati karenaGw mengirim 25 koneksi ke port 22 dalam hitungan detik.

nodes.label: An empty list endpoint hides an object that get-by-id finds
nodes.norm_label: an empty list endpoint hides an object that get by id finds
nodes.summary: The Civo account's GET /v2/instances returned an empty array, which the agent read as 'the account owns no instances' and acted on for a long stretch. The instance was there the whole time: GET /v2/instances/{id}?region=jkt1 returned it (fbee98aa-0ed0-440f-aa7d-c5603dca0f3a, public_ip 49.128.191.153, matching the VPS). A second discriminator also mattered: probing the console endpoint returned database_operation_find rather than database_instance_not_found, a different error meaning the instance was found but no console session existed. The note states plainly that the user was right and the agent was wrong.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - koneksi-vps-banyak-packet-loss [ses_f1c7fa998ffeaX7rILtty0alcT].md:L04890] `GET /v2/instances` memang bohong kosong, tapi `GET /v2/instances/{id}?region=jkt1`JORGE ada.

nodes.label: Opening a Civo VNC console session with PUT vnc plus an API-key-to-JWT exchange
nodes.norm_label: opening a civo vnc console session with put vnc plus an api key to jwt exchange
nodes.summary: The out-of-band access path used to reach a VPS whose SSH was banned. Three steps written into a script: PUT https://api.civo.com/v2/instances/{id}/vnc?region=jkt1&duration=1h returns a noVNC uri (idempotent while the session lives); POST https://api.civo.com/v2/auth/exchange with the API key as the Authorization header returns {access_token}; the JWT is appended to the uri as a token parameter. The agent deliberately kept the token out of chat and wrote the URL to a file instead. Firewall rules for the instance were also read via the API: all 12 rules were action allow for 0.0.0.0/0 with no deny rule, which located the block inside the instance rather than in the cloud firewall.

nodes.label: Inbound port scan flooding the kernel log as the explanation for the packet loss
nodes.norm_label: inbound port scan flooding the kernel log as the explanation for the packet loss
nodes.summary: The console that appeared to show only logs was showing a kernel ring buffer full of [UFW BLOCK] lines with random source IPs and random destination ports (3306, 6008, 22674, 8080, 41779, 55003 and so on). Because ufw with default deny incoming writes every blocked packet to /dev/console, an internet-wide scan buried the login prompt. The same flood was offered as the real answer to the original question: constant inbound scan traffic saturates the instance NIC and conntrack table, raising CPU and dropping packets, which fits both the 16-20 percent loss and its correlation with latency spikes. The proposed mitigations were ufw limit 22/tcp instead of allow, and ufw logging low.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - koneksi-vps-banyak-packet-loss [ses_f1c7fa998ffeaX7rILtty0alcT].md:L5536] Massive inbound scan traffic saturates the instance NIC/conntrack, producing high CPU and dropped packets, which explains the 16-20 percent loss and the jitter and why loss correlates with latency spikes.

nodes.label: fail2ban bans survive a reboot because expiry is absolute in its sqlite database
nodes.norm_label: fail2ban bans survive a reboot because expiry is absolute in sqlite
nodes.summary: This is why the console instruction ordered systemctl disable --now fail2ban before dmesg -n 1. fail2ban stores bans in /var/lib/fail2ban/fail2ban.sqlite3 with an absolute expiry timestamp, so a reboot reloads them rather than clearing them; silencing the screen first would have tidied the display while changing nothing about the block. Disabling the daemon fixes two things at once: the agent's own ban disappears immediately, and the UFW BLOCK flood stops because nothing is writing to /dev/console. The ban was confirmed still live after reboot by checking from other vantage points: 49.128.191.153:22 still refused from the agent at 23:13 while Hong Kong (0.05 s) and the UK (0.17 s) connected directly, which showed the machine was healthy and only 182.10.168.104 was being rejected.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - koneksi-vps-banyak-packet-loss [ses_f1c7fa998ffeaX7rILtty0alcT].md:L06275] Alasannya: fail2ban menyimpan ban-nya di `/var/lib/fail2ban/fail2ban.sqlite3` dengan **waktu kedaluwarsa absolut**, jadi **reboot tidak menghapusnya** — dia cuma dimuat ulang saat daemon start.

nodes.label: Soft reboot left the console 503; the hard reboot restored it
nodes.norm_label: soft reboot left the console 503 hard reboot restored it
nodes.summary: POST /v2/instances/{id}/soft_reboots returned {result: success} and the instance status stayed ACTIVE throughout, which is indistinguishable from a no-op when observed only from outside. The console then answered 503 with a valid token: authentication passed but the QEMU backend was not there. DELETE plus PUT of the session did not help. POST /v2/instances/{id}/reboots (hard) showed a real state transition, SHUTOFF at 23:11:32 then ACTIVE at 23:11:54, and the noVNC page afterwards returned 200 with 15403 bytes of valid HTML. The agent flagged that it could not prove the soft reboot had happened at all, since API success and a real reboot look the same from outside.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - koneksi-vps-banyak-packet-loss [ses_f1c7fa998ffeaX7rILtty0alcT].md:L6616] The soft reboot returned success but never left ACTIVE and the console stayed 503; the hard reboot showed SHUTOFF then ACTIVE and the noVNC page then answered 200.

nodes.label: RED proved by reverting the implementation to HEAD while leaving the new tests in place
nodes.norm_label: red proved by reverting the implementation to head while leaving the new tests in place
nodes.summary: The task asked for tests written first and a recorded behaviour-assertion failure. The agent instead implemented first and manufactured the RED afterwards: back up the two implementation files to /tmp, git checkout -- them back to HEAD, run both suites, restore, and verify byte-identical with sha256sum -c. The test files were never reverted, so the failure was the new tests meeting the old code. Recorded result: platform-client.test.mjs 18 failed / 8 passed of 26 with the RED run naming all three CARGO_PKG_VERSION sites by line (273, 410, 421), and useWhatsNew.test.ts 9 failed / 12 passed of 21.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - t9-desktop-client-rollback-and-notes [ses_f1d47e559ffeBDJdSCNlh6VfcV].md:L9762] Implemented first, then backed up the implementation, git checkout -- to HEAD, ran both suites and restored, verified byte-identical; the test files were never reverted so the failures were behaviour assertions against unfixed code.

nodes.label: A missing-export TypeError is not acceptable RED proof
nodes.norm_label: a missing export typeerror is not acceptable red proof
nodes.summary: Of the 9 failing web tests in the RED run, 7 failed with TypeError: selectBundledHighlights is not a function or detectReleasePlatform is not a function. Those are missing exports, so the test never reached the behaviour. The agent flagged them as such in the report rather than counting them, and identified the two that do carry behavioural proof: a Linux client received the three Windows-only 0.6.838 notes (expected [...] to deeply equal []), and the request carried no target at all (expected null to be 'linux'). The task prompt had already set this rule, stating that a missing-import or parse error is not acceptable RED proof.

nodes.label: A single shared with_platform_query builder for every updater request
nodes.norm_label: a single shared with platform query builder for every updater request
nodes.summary: The updater commands needed target OS and architecture on every version-list, previous-version and rollback URL so the worker could pick a channel. Rather than appending parameters at each of the three call sites, one function with_platform_query(endpoint, scope) appends target= and arch= and picks ? or & based on whether the endpoint already carries a query. Its stated purpose is structural: a new endpoint cannot accidentally be added without the platform scope. release_channel_for_target_os maps windows/linux/android to the worker's channel names and returns None for anything else. Tests assert the exact URLs, that exactly one ? appears, and that the parameter names extracted from the Rust source are exactly target and arch.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - t9-desktop-client-rollback-and-notes [ses_f1d47e559ffeBDJdSCNlh6VfcV].md:L5702] One builder for every request, so a new endpoint cannot accidentally be added without the platform scope.

nodes.label: Honest empty state instead of another platform's notes
nodes.norm_label: honest empty state instead of another platforms notes
nodes.summary: apps/web/src/data/changelog.ts is generated from the Windows records only, because the desktop app ships no Linux or Android bundle. So a non-Windows client must never read the bundled array at all, and selectBundledHighlights returns an empty array whenever the detected platform is not the platform the bundle was generated for. selectRemoteHighlights refuses three ways: no platform, a payload that is not an object, and a version that is not the one being shown. detectReleasePlatform returning null is also not a fallback to Windows; when the user agent names no known platform no request is sent at all.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - t9-desktop-client-rollback-and-notes [ses_f1d47e559ffeBDJdSCNlh6VfcV].md:L3310] Honest empty state: refuse rather than fall back to another platform's notes, because a wrong guess hands a Linux client Windows release notes.

nodes.label: changelog.ts output shape frozen by the sync check comparing whole file text
nodes.norm_label: generated changelog shape frozen by the sync check comparing whole file text
nodes.summary: T9 was tempted to add a platform field to changelog.ts. It did not, because sync-app-changelog.mjs check regenerates the file from generateChangelogTs(...) and compares the whole text, so any shape change would break docs:check-app-changelog. T12 had deliberately left the platform field out. The file ended the task byte-untouched with an empty git diff --stat, and the Windows projection was asserted three executed ways instead: syncAppChangelog with checkOnly true, CHANGELOG_RELEASES deep-equalling the Windows extraction, and selectPlatformEntries for linux and android returning an empty array.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - t9-desktop-client-rollback-and-notes [ses_f1d47e559ffeBDJdSCNlh6VfcV].md:L3416] check regenerates from the fixed template, so adding a platform field would fail it; the file was kept unchanged as the Windows compatibility view.

nodes.label: An equal version number must not make two platforms interchangeable
nodes.norm_label: an equal version number must not make two platforms interchangeable
nodes.summary: Windows and Linux advance independently, so the same version number on two platforms is two different releases. The Rust test an_equal_version_number_does_not_make_two_platforms_interchangeable asserts the version-list URL, the previous-version URL and the exact-rollback URL all differ between a Windows x86_64 scope and a Linux x86_64 scope at 0.6.900, and the web side has the matching case two_platforms_at_the_same_version_produce_different_urls. This was the isolation the whole change exists for, and its RED evidence was a Linux client actually receiving the three Windows-only 0.6.838 notes.

nodes.label: Omitting the platform for a target with no release line beats adding an error code outside the allowlist
nodes.norm_label: an omitted legacy view beats a new error code outside the allowlist
nodes.summary: A hard error looked more in the spirit of the design's clause that an invalid explicit OS fails rather than silently selecting Windows. It was rejected on the note's own reasoning: the design's failure clause is about explicit OS values, and a client that cannot name an OS is the legacy path by design (old unqualified previous and versions requests resolve to the historical Windows compatibility view). Erroring would also have required editing error_codes.rs, which was outside the allowlist. The chosen behaviour is that release_channel_for_target_os returns None, with_platform_query sends no parameters at all and logs a warning, and the test asserts the omission produces exactly the legacy URL. The agent listed this as a deliberate fallback on a path no shipping target can reach.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - t9-desktop-client-rollback-and-notes [ses_f1d47e559ffeBDJdSCNlh6VfcV].md:L5677] A client that cannot name an OS is the legacy path by design; erroring would need error_codes.rs, outside the allowlist, so the parameters are omitted and a warning logged.

nodes.label: Tauri's {{target}} placeholder expands to target_os(), not a target triple
nodes.norm_label: tauri target placeholder expands to target os not a triple
nodes.summary: Found while verifying the client against the worker. RELEASE_CHANNELS holds bare channel names, so a target triple such as x86_64-pc-windows-msvc or windows-x86_64 is a 400 at the worker rather than a silent Windows selection. Tauri expands {{target}} to its own target_os() string (windows or linux) per updater.rs:449-452 in tauri-plugin-updater-2.12.0, so the pre-existing latest.json endpoint in tauri.conf.json is already compatible and the Rust builder must never produce a triple. A test asserts the worker rejects the triples and accepts the bare names.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - t9-desktop-client-rollback-and-notes [ses_f1d47e559ffeBDJdSCNlh6VfcV].md:L9854] RELEASE_CHANNELS holds bare channel names so a triple is a 400 there, and Tauri expands {{target}} to its own target_os() string, which is why the configured endpoint is already compatible.

nodes.label: rustfmt parse check proves syntax, not types or borrows
nodes.norm_label: rustfmt parse check proves syntax not types or borrows
nodes.summary: The suite cannot compile Rust, and cargo is forbidden on this host, so the only Rust verification obtainable was rustfmt --edition 2021 --emit stdout, which exited 0 and produced a byte-identical file. The report states that this proves the syntax is valid and that cargo fmt --check will pass, and that it proves nothing about types, borrow-checking, or the assertions themselves. Behavioural Rust tests asserting exact URLs and the user-agent value were written but have never been compiled or run. The report names the exact cargo commands the parent must run on vps-bcb and separates executed evidence from source-level-only claims, listing the uncompiled Rust half as the single biggest risk.

nodes.label: Debian's generic Login incorrect refuses user enumeration
nodes.norm_label: debian login incorrect refuses user enumeration
nodes.summary: The console rejected the bcb login and the agent read the message as meaning either the user does not exist or the password is wrong. The note explains Debian deliberately uses one message for both so it cannot be used to enumerate users, and adds that root would not work either because PermitRootLogin prohibit-password from the instance user-data refuses password login for root by every method including the console. That stopped the guessing: two failures were treated as enough, because an active pam_faillock locks the account at five.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - koneksi-vps-banyak-packet-loss [ses_f1c7fa998ffeaX7rILtty0alcT].md:L7155] Debian sengaja memakai pesan yang sama untuk keduanya supaya tidak bisa dipakai enumerate user, dan dua percobaan gagal sudah cukup karena pam_faillock mengunci akun pada lima kali.

nodes.label: Connection refused in 51 ms is a TCP reset, not a dropped packet
nodes.norm_label: connection refused in 51 ms is a tcp reset not a dropped packet
nodes.summary: ECONNREFUSED on 49.128.191.153:22 after 51 ms. The 51 ms is what carries the information: a reset came back fast, so something was actively rejecting the IP rather than packets being dropped silently, which is what distinguishes a REJECT from a DROP and rules out a plain firewall timeout. The note uses this to refuse to guess the fail2ban bantime, listing one hour, one day and one week as the live possibilities and saying outright that it does not know.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - koneksi-vps-banyak-packet-loss [ses_f1c7fa998ffeaX7rILtty0alcT].md:L7847] ECONNREFUSED dalam 51 ms adalah RST, bukan timeout, jadi ada yang aktif menolak IP itu, bukan paket yang di-drop diam-diam.
